summary: The checked-out kernel still wrote expert_start_loc with a masked subset of lanes and immediately reloaded it without a CTA barrier. gfx950 compiler output preserved that store/reload dependency. The kernel now derives each expert offset from the already-loaded token counts, eliminating the unsynchronized global-memory communication. A regression rejects reintroducing the reload and GPU reference tests cover empty experts, padding, multiple block sizes, and non-power-of-two expert counts.

tests.command: HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 TRITON_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/amdpilot-repo-j-a22f70b60735/triton-cache python -m pytest -q test/registered/kernels/ops/moe/test_ep_scatter.py::test_ep_scatter_prefix_is_not_reloaded (with the original source restored temporarily)
tests.what_was_measured: Failing-before regression: detected tl.load(expert_start_loc + cur_expert) after the prefix store. Raw output: /tmp/amdpilot-repo-j-a22f70b60735/evidence/pytest_ep_scatter_before.txt

Five passing regression/reference cases on gfx950: no prefix reload plus exact prefix and m_indices results for zero counts, partially valid padded blocks, block sizes 32/64/128, and 1/3/5/17 experts. Raw output: /tmp/amdpilot-repo-j-a22f70b60735/evidence/pytest_ep_scatter_after.txt

200 guarded GPU launches matched an independent PyTorch prefix/index reference with zero failures; generated TTIR contained no cur_expert_start reload. Raw output and compiler artifacts: /tmp/amdpilot-repo-j-a22f70b60735/evidence/postfix_probe.txt and postfix_kernel.{ttir,ttgir,llir,amdgcn}.
Repository formatting, lint, syntax, and registered-test metadata checks passed. Raw output: /tmp/amdpilot-repo-j-a22f70b60735/evidence/pre_commit.txt

remaining_limitations: The reported intermittent numerical/illegal-access symptom did not occur in 200 guarded launches on gfx950, although the compiler output confirmed the unsafe store/reload dependency.
The reporter used an NVIDIA H20 with CUDA/PTX; no NVIDIA GPU was assigned, so the exact PTX and H20 scheduling behavior were not reproduced.

No model weights or multi-node DeepEP environment were available, so the reported end-to-end CPU recv timeout path was not reproduced. The focused test validates only this Triton kernel's prefix/index output and compiler dataflow.
No native C++ or FlyDSL source changed, so no native rebuild was applicable.
